### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **47** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fbe012729ce47777e47a0bd9ac816a3d4763fe3d` — the merge of head `ec7d6af8b8b7e75fc2e7d61e29a3dcf15e350ab4` into base `b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fbe012729ce47777e47a0bd9ac816a3d4763fe3d && git checkout fbe012729ce47777e47a0bd9ac816a3d4763fe3d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214 ec7d6af8b8b7e75fc2e7d61e29a3dcf15e350ab4 && git checkout -B drift-repro b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214 && git merge --no-ff ec7d6af8b8b7e75fc2e7d61e29a3dcf15e350ab4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b9ac35cbfe60afcea88947ed4eaf8c50e3efc214` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The gate families the brief lists are all answered green by these.

### ① Derived judgments

**The by-name read, `getMetaItem` (protocol.ts).** The tail added after `readMetaItem` is right on every axis the triage answer fixes.
- Type exemption. `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` folds the spelling before the check, so `objects` and `packages` reach `request.type === 'object' || 'package'` singular; the `apps` READERS row pins the fold for the hidden side. `object` keeps its pre-check refusal `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` (unchanged from #24208); `package` is never hidden. Matches triage ("absence for a non-object type; `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` stays the object answer").
- One predicate (H1). `isItemOfDisabledPackage` asks `registry.isPackageDisabled(item._packageId)` of the item the read RESOLVED, after `mergeArtifactProtection` grafted the envelope package chosen by `envelopePackageId`. Every layer carries that field: the stored row (`package_id` grafted at step 1 and on the draft arm), the registry item (stamped by `registerItem`), the artifact. The list filter (`readFlattenedMetaItems`) now calls the same helper on its merged items, which carry `_packageId` from the package slot (line 10114, `held._packageId === undefined ? {...held, _packageId: pkg}`). A package-unbound stored row overlaying a disabled package's code item is hidden on both reads for the same reason. `registry.isPackageDisabled(undefined)` is `false`, so an unowned item is served by both. Right.
- The absence shape (H2). Active and `previewDrafts`: the answer is the envelope with `item: undefined` and `registration` dropped. The strict draft read throws `noPendingDraftError`, the one constructor the missing-draft branch now shares (message, code and status identical; pinned). Both transports judge absence on `item == null`: REST's `createMetaItemAnswer` judges absence BEFORE the per-caller gate (#18066) and renders `sendMetaItemAbsent`; the REST cached arm (`getMetaItemCached` throws on a falsy item) reaches the same emitter; the dispatcher's `data?.item != null` hit test falls to the service fallback, whose new guard nulls the copy, and the branch ends at its own `deps.error('Not found', 404)`. The missing name takes the identical exits. Byte identity is pinned on the dispatcher and measured on REST. Right.
- The envelope kept (Q4). `lock`, `editable`, `deletable`, `resettable`, `version`, `packageId` and the rest stay. No transport serialises an item-less envelope (REST: the absent body; dispatcher: its 404), so nothing new reaches the wire. Its two in-process readers are the CLI ceremony and plugin-security, below. Right.
- The list filter's refactor is behaviour-identical on `SchemaRegistry`; the one difference is that a registry WITHOUT `isPackageDisabled` no longer throws from the list read and hides nothing. A degenerate-host widening only, and the same optional-call shape `isObjectOfDisabledPackage` already has. Named, accepted.

**The dispatcher (meta.ts), four doors, cross-lane to `domain:cli`.**
- `/meta/object/NAME/state/FIELD`: `disabledObjectAnswer` runs before `registry.getObject`; it asks `isObjectPackageDisabled(name)` (a non-object name answers false and the door proceeds), then reads the protocol's own refusal and renders it through `errorFromThrown` as `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. A host whose protocol does not refuse gets the door's own `404 Object not found`. The protocol read's body is discarded, so no schema is disclosed. Pinned: `getObject` is never asked the name. Right.
- The legacy one-segment `/meta/NAME` exit: the same helper, placed after the anonymous deny and before `registry.getObject`; reachable only on a host whose protocol declares no type set (`refuseUnknownMetaListType` answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` first on a real composition, enabled and disabled alike, as measured). Closed in code and pinned with that host shape. Right.
- `/meta/:type/:name/published`: the blanket `catch` now re-throws `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` instead of falling through to `getPublished`; pinned (`getPublished` never called). REST's twin re-throws any status-bearing throw (`typeof overlayError?.status === 'number'`, line 8202), so for this code the two transports agree; the dispatcher still swallows OTHER status-bearing throws into the snapshot, a pre-existing parity gap outside this card. Right for the card; the gap is named only.
- The non-object item read's metadata-service fallback: `isServiceItemOfDisabledPackage` asks the engine registry's `isPackageDisabled` of the service copy's `_packageId`, `package` exempt. Without it the dispatcher would have served the service's copy where the protocol said absent. Pinned byte-identical to the missing name. Right.

**REST (rest-server.ts), `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` only (ruling item 1).** The member is reached from exactly two places, `eventDoorRefusal` (`/history`, `/audit`) and the `/diff` branch, and only for `gatesPerCaller` types: `book`, `doc`, `app`, `view`, `dashboard`. `object` never reaches it. With item 1 alone, a withheld item read as "no current document" and `eventDoorRefusal` returned `undefined`, so events and a view's or dashboard's diff were served to a caller the item's own gate refuses: a bypass this PR would have created, measured 200 before and 404 after on the gated author. The fix throws the plain read's absence when `getMetaItemLayered.effective` is non-null; a deleted item (every layer null) keeps `undefined` and its old answer. I checked for other cases where the plain read serves no item while `effective` resolves: the only bundled type is `email_template` (not gated); `isAppPackageIdKey` returns earlier; a rowless expanded view is served by the plain read. So for the gated types the branch fires on a disable alone. The throw is rendered by the doors' `handleRouteError` (`resolveErrorResponse`): status 404, code `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, the flat body. Right; the body dialect is flag ③.1. For ungated types (`page`, `flow`, `report`, ...) the event and diff doors still serve a disabled package's item's events and diff: no gate exists to bypass, and events outliving the item is the doors' existing design for a deleted item; the rest changeset's "Absent now" list names the gated types only, honestly. Named, accepted.

**plugin-security, `readServedPackageBinding` only (ruling item 2).** The envelope's `packageId` is `servedLockState`'s, which is `extractProtection(decorated).packageId`, which is `decorated._packageId`: the same field of the same served document the function read before as `item._packageId`. So the enabled case is unchanged byte for byte and the disabled case keeps the binding. The existence decision stays with `getMetaItemLayered` (untouched); no enforcement change, no new public method. Pinned on the REAL protocol with anti-vacuity (the item is withheld, the echo still records `_packageId`, and stays owned after the re-enable); the stub double now mirrors `servedLockState`. Right.

**Blast radius, every in-repo caller of `getMetaItem` at the head.** Object-only callers, unchanged: core `import-runner`, rest `import-prepare`, `data-action-routes`, `rest-server` 2652 (`loadObjectItem` gate input), 8429, 8472, service-automation 364, plugin-auth (`sys_user` field coercion), the protocol's seed adapter (25453), meta.ts's object branch. Non-object callers, each now reads absence and none must tell disabled from missing: rest `import-mapping` and service-automation `connector-pull` (`mapping`: `404 MAPPING_NOT_FOUND`, right, a disabled package's mapping must not drive an import or a pull); runtime `applyPublishedSeeds` (`seed`: the response's `seedApplied.errors[]` names the unreadable seed, and the data plane refuses its objects regardless); service-analytics' pending-seed probe (`NO_DRAFT` already caught, no pending rows); the protocol's build probes (26607, best-effort, swallowed); `getMetaItemCached` (the REST cached arm, absent). The CLI ownership ceremony's `lock.verdict` reads `editable`, `lock` and `lockReason` only, never `item`, so the kept envelope gives it the same verdict; it enumerates through `getMetaItems`, which already omits these items. No resolution reader is blinded: the registry's `getObject` and `listItems` are untouched, the save's destructive-change check still reads `readMetaItem`, the echo's existence read is the layered read, and the lock gate's verdict rides the kept envelope. objectui's `probeMetaItemAccess` maps the absent 404 to `not_found` (`isMetaItemAbsentError`), `getPage` and friends to `null`, as the PR's premise table says. The REST per-caller gate's inputs are the list read and the item's own keys, and absence is judged before the gate, so no gate input changes.

**What each door answers now** (disabled package's item | triage's answer | a missing name):
- `getMetaItem` active and `previewDrafts`, every type but `object`/`package`: no `item`, envelope kept | absence | no `item`, envelope kept.
- `getMetaItem` `state: 'draft'`: `404 NO_DRAFT`, the missing draft's message | absence | `404 NO_DRAFT`.
- REST `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME` (plain, cached, `?preview=draft`): `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, nested body | absence | identical bytes.
- Dispatcher `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME`: `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` "Not found" | absence | identical bytes (pinned).
- Objects on every by-name face, both transports: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` | the object answer | `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
- Dispatcher `/meta/object/NAME/state/FIELD`: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` | the object answer | `404 Object not found`.
- Dispatcher one-segment `/meta/NAME`: `400 INVALID_REQUEST` on a real composition; `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` where the exit is reachable | the object answer | `404 Not found`.
- `/meta/object/NAME/published`, both transports: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` | the object answer | 404.
- REST `/meta/TYPE/NAME/history`, `/audit`, `/diff`, gated types (`app`, `view`, `dashboard`, `doc`, `book`): `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, flat body | absence (status and code) | events, or `/diff`'s absence for `app`/`doc`/`book`, as before.
- Stopped, still serving, named in the PR body and the changesets: non-object `?layers=true`, `/layers` and `/published` on both transports; REST `/meta/object/NAME/state/FIELD` (reads `ql.registry.getObject` at line 7947); `GET /meta/_drafts`; the ungated types' event and diff doors.

### ② Semver level

- Three breaking changesets (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/rest`), each `minor`, each marked **BREAKING** with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `minor` is the launch-window level `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces for a breaking change ("During the launch window we ship breaking changes as minor"); `no-migration-prescription` is in that gate's `CATEGORIES` (line 539), and its reasoning holds: no stored metadata changes shape, no key, export or code is added or removed, re-enabling restores the read. Each body states what was served and what is answered now, and the one-line remedy. The runtime changeset's `/published` bullet names objects only and the rest changeset's "Absent now" names the gated types only; both match the diff.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`, no `Clause-②` line, no marker: right. Relative to `main` the echo's observable behaviour is unchanged (an in-PR repair of what the narrowing alone would have broken; `packageId` is the same document field); it is a published-source change, so `patch` is the minimum a changeset may carry.
- No `@objectstack/objectql` changeset: its diff is a test file outside the published `files`. Right.
- The PR body's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the repo spelling of triage's "yes (narrowing)" (AGENTS.md: `yes` means a new key on a published payload; this diff adds none; `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm). The title carries `!`. The face is narrowing, hence this tier.
- CI's verdict: `Check Changeset` `success` on both passes (that job runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base MERGE_BASE`, pr-automation.yml lines 977 and 1127).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Flat vs nested 404 body on the event and diff doors** (report 2, open question; app `/diff` moves from nested to flat). Answered, not a blocker: the plain read's contract is status plus code (ADR-0112 minimum, which the pin asserts), and both match; the body dialect is the one those doors already speak for every throw (`handleRouteError`). Escalated as a door-side follow-up item on the card, beside item 3's doors (recommendation A: render through `sendMetaItemAbsent` in `eventDoorRefusal` and the `/diff` branch), for the seat to fold into that dispatch.
2. **Interim REST `/meta/object/NAME/state/FIELD` split** (Q2): accepted by ruling 6241893667 item 4, named in the PR body, claimed by no changeset. REST serves a disabled object's FSM introspection (`next` states from the schema, no rows) until its half lands. Notice 6243012505 says no `/meta` move series is pending any more, so the REST half can be dispatched at the seat's discretion rather than after slice 13e. Not a blocker.
3. **Non-object `?layers=true`, `/layers`, `/published` on both transports** (Q1): ruling A stands; the producer `getMetaItemLayered` keeps serving the echo (a resolution reader), the doors close door-side. Lead for that dispatch: `MetadataManager.getPublished`'s document carries no `_packageId`, so the door needs the name's owner from the registry or the layered envelope's `packageId`. The body's `Part of #24210` is therefore right, and the "Part-of PR must not also close its card" check is `success`.
4. **The envelope kept** (Q4): ruling A, verified above; no transport serialises it, the CLI reads only lock fields. Answered.
5. **`GET /meta/_drafts` lists a disabled package's drafts while the by-name draft read answers `NO_DRAFT`** (out-of-scope finding 1): ruling item 6 folds it into item 3's follow-up. Meanwhile Studio's `DraftChangesPanel` lists such a draft and reads both sides as null. Answered.
6. **The echo binding** (out-of-scope finding 2): fixed in this PR under ruling item 2, verified with anti-vacuity. Answered.
7. **Ungated types' event and diff doors** still serve a disabled package's item's events and diff: not a gate bypass (no per-caller gate), consistent with the deleted-item design, honestly scoped in the rest changeset. Named; nothing owed.
8. **`seed` and `mapping` callers read absence now**: consistent with triage's "no caller must tell disabled from missing"; the seed-apply response names the unreadable seed. Named; nothing owed.
9. **List filter's optional call**: a degenerate-host widening only (a registry without the predicate hides nothing instead of throwing); the pin runs the real `SchemaRegistry`. Named; nothing owed.
10. **Dev deviations**: `Part of` over the dispatch's `Fixes` (os-dev.md's DoD wins; right, doors remain open); the round-1 objectql typecheck miss (TS2367) is fixed in the head commit and CI is green; the dispatcher was measured through `createHonoApp`'s fetch handler, not a socket (no in-repo host mounts it over one; acceptable); the PR body was re-worded to the head (`27 types; the schema does not list package`). The dispatcher `/published` re-throw being narrower than REST's for other status-bearing throws is pre-existing and outside this card.
11. **CI**: nothing in progress, nothing failed; the skipped runs are path and opt-in filters, and no exported symbol moves, so the Console Pin Gate's skip is not a gap.
